title: A flat quasi-finite slice through a closed Cohen–Macaulay fibre point
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a flat morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $s\in S$ and let $x$ be a closed point [def-weil-closed-points] of the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Suppose that $R=\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $\operatorname{depth}R=\dim R$ [def-weil-pbc-depth, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Then there are a scheme $Z$, a morphism $i:Z\to X$, and a point $z\in Z_s$ such that $i(z)=x$, the composite $f\circ i:Z\to S$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, and $Z_s$ has exactly one point, namely $z$. Moreover $f\circ i$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite].

source.place: Tag 0570, label lemma-slice-CM, specialized to a globally flat morphism and forgetting regularity of the immersion in its conclusion

proof.text: We prove a slightly stronger induction claim: for every flat locally finitely presented $g:Y\to S$, every closed $y\in Y_s$ with Noetherian fibre local ring $A$ satisfying $\operatorname{depth}(A)\ge\dim A$, there is a slice with all the conclusions of the item. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-finite-krull-dimension], $d=\dim A$ is a finite nonnegative integer. Induct strongly on $d$, uniformly over $g,Y,S,s,y$. The original hypotheses imply this induction hypothesis at $g=f,y=x$, since equality implies the required inequality. The strengthening permits exactly the depth inequality supplied by the quotient lemma below.

source.place: Tag 0570, lemma-slice-CM, induction setup; use local-ring dimension as the induction parameter.

proof.text: Suppose $d=0$. Choose affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}C\subseteq S$ containing $s$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Y$ containing $y$, with $g(U)\subseteq V$ and $C\to B$ finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. In particular it is finite type. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $U_s=\operatorname{Spec}F$ with $F=B\otimes_C\kappa(s)$; the images of any finite set of algebra generators of $B$ generate $F$ over $\kappa(s)$. The point $y$ is closed in $U_s$, hence corresponds to a maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $F$, and $F_{\mathfrak n}=A$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-dimension-local-ring] gives $\dim_y\operatorname{Spec}F=\dim A=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-quasifinite-zero-fibre-dimension] to $C\to B$ at the prime of $y$: it is quasi-finite at that prime. The affine pair $(U,V)$ therefore makes $g$ quasi-finite at $y$ by [pqf-def-quasifinite].

source.place: Tag 0570, lemma-slice-CM, case d=0; Tag 0397, morphisms-lemma-locally-quasi-finite-rel-dimension-0; Tag 00OU, algebra-lemma-dimension-closed-point-finite-type-field.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-quasi-finite-points-open], the quasi-finite locus is an open neighbourhood $W$ of $y$ and $W\to S$ is locally quasi-finite. The map $g$ is locally of finite type because its local finite presentations give finitely many algebra generators. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-point-isolated] makes $\{y\}$ open in $Y_s$. By the subspace-topology assertion of [def-pc-scheme-fibre], choose an open $O\subseteq Y$ with $O\cap Y_s=\{y\}$. Put $Z=O\cap W$ with its open-subscheme structure and take $i:Z\to Y$ to be the inclusion; then $Z_s=\{y\}$. The restriction is locally quasi-finite by [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-restriction-to-opens]. It is flat because the stalk rings and their maps are unchanged on an open subscheme [def-weil-flat-morphism]. It is locally finitely presented: inside each finitely presented affine chart, principal opens form a basis; if $B=C[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/(P_1,\ldots,P_m)$ and $b$ is represented by $Q(t)$, then $B_b=C[t_1,\ldots,t_r,u]/(P_1,\ldots,P_m,uQ-1)$. These principal charts cover the restriction and give its finite presentations [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. This finishes the base case.

source.place: Tag 0570, lemma-slice-CM, zero-dimensional case; Tag 01TI, morphisms-lemma-quasi-finite-points-open; Tag 01K1, schemes-lemma-fibre-topological.

proof.text: Now let $d>0$. By [def-weil-pbc-depth], the inequality $\operatorname{depth}(A)\ge d>0$ implies that there is a nonempty regular sequence in the maximal ideal of $A$: otherwise the supremum of its possible lengths would be zero. Its first element $\bar h$ is a nonzerodivisor in that maximal ideal by [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. By [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient], $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\twoheadrightarrow A$ is the quotient by $\mathfrak m_s\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. Lift $\bar h$ to $h\in\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. This lift lies in the maximal ideal: a unit would have unit image in the nonzero local ring $A$, whereas $\bar h$ is in its maximal ideal. Since $g$ is flat at $y$ and locally finitely presented, [lem-trf-fibre-regular-element-flat-hypersurface] supplies an affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $y$, a representative $a$ of $h$, and $D=\operatorname{Spec}(B/(a))\subseteq U$ containing $y$, such that $D\to S$ is flat and locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Tags 0570 and 056Z, lemma-slice-CM and lemma-slice-once; Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element.

proof.text: Write $y_D$ for the point of $D_s$ mapping to $y$. The affine definition of the closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] and the fibre stalk quotient [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient] identify its local ring as $A_D=A/(\bar h)$. Explicitly, if $T=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, the local ring of $D$ is $T/(h)$: localization commutes with quotient by sending $b/t\bmod a$ to $(b\bmod a)/(t\bmod a)$, with inverse given by the same fraction before quotient. Its fibre local ring is therefore $(T/(h))/\mathfrak m_s(T/(h))=T/(h,\mathfrak m_sT)=(T/\mathfrak m_sT)/(\bar h)=A/(\bar h)$. These identifications send the original germ to its named class. The point $y_D$ is closed in $D_s$, since $D_s\to U_s$ is the closed subscheme cut out by the image of $a$ (the same quotient computation on affine charts), and $y$ is closed in $Y_s$.

source.place: Tag 0570, lemma-slice-CM, local-ring identification in the induction step; Tag 0HA1, schemes-lemma-local-ring-fibre.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cm-local-quotient-nonzerodivisor-cm] to $A$ and $\bar h$. Its hypotheses hold: $A$ is Noetherian local of finite dimension $d$, has depth at least $d$, and $\bar h$ is a nonzerodivisor in its maximal ideal. It follows that $A_D$ is Noetherian local, $\dim A_D=d-1$, and $\operatorname{depth}(A_D)\ge d-1$. Thus the induction claim applies to the flat locally finitely presented map $D\to S$ and the closed point $y_D\in D_s$. It yields $j:Z\to D$ and $z\in Z_s$ mapping to $y_D$, with $Z_s=\{z\}$ and $Z\to S$ flat, locally finitely presented and locally quasi-finite. Compose $j$ with $D\to U\to Y$ to obtain $i:Z\to Y$. The structural morphism $Z\to S$ is exactly the one supplied by induction, so all its three properties persist without any assertion that the immersion itself is flat. Its singleton fibre point maps to $y$. This proves the induction step and, with the first step, proves the item.

source.place: Tag 0570, lemma-slice-CM, positive-dimensional induction; Tag 02JN, algebra-lemma-reformulate-CM. Regularity of the final immersion is not required by this item.
